To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
alpha-methylserotonin excites barosensitive neurons in the rostral VLM, and that this excitation is blocked by the 5-HT-2 receptor antagonist ketanserin.
alpha-methyl5-HT excited 69% of neurones tested and inhibited 31% of neurones in the RVLM.
5-HT2 receptors in the RVLM are excitatory and that 5-HT1A receptors are inhibitory.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role played by the 5-HT receptor in the central nervous system.
the central control of blood pressure and the role of the rostral ventral lateral medulla (RVLM) in this process.
the role of serotonin (5-hydroxytryptamine, 5-HT) in the central nervous system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of alpha-methyl 5-HT are complex and depend on the dose and the site of application.

the 5-HT1A receptor agonist 8-OH-DPAT, the 5-HT3 receptor agonist m-chlorophenylbiguanide and the 5-HT4 receptor agonist 5-methoxytryptamine all excite neurones in the nucleus tractus solitarii and that the 5-HT1A and 5-HT2 receptors mediate these excitations.
alpha-methyl 5-HT is a potent agonist at both 5-HT1 and 5-HT2 receptors and is a partial agonist at 5-HT3 receptors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
alpha-methylserotonin is a potent excitatory agonist at 5-HT2A receptors and an agonist of the 5-hydroxytryptamine 2C receptor.
the rostral ventral lateral medullary neurone population is heterogeneous with respect to 5-HT2 agonist responses.
the 5-HT system is involved in the control of blood pressure, and that this effect is due to a 5-HT2 mediated action on the rostral ventral lateral medulla.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have identified a novel role for 5-HT2 receptors in the RVLM.
the 5-HT receptor system is a complex and multifaceted network that can be used to regulate the cardiovascular system.
the 5-HT 2A receptor agonists are effective at stimulating dopamine neurons, but that they do not appear to be selective for this action.
